name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,677

clue.text: Antipodean's able to eat trout regularly and this for dessert?

definitions.note: 'this' stands for the answer itself, something served as a pudding

indicators.note: doing something regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter is kept
whatever eats something takes it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a Kiwi is a New Zealander, an Antipodean; the 's is 'is'
fit and able: capable
second and fourth letters of the fish

explanation.surface: A New Zealander is ready to tuck into some trout, and wonders what pudding will follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat' looks like the Antipodean's dinner, but it is the able word doing the eating. The clue is semi-&lit: 'this' points back at the answer as a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuzzy-skinned green fruit native to China but famously grown in New Zealand is commonly eaten as a sweet course.

clue.text: Plan change when Democrat ousts Republican

indicators.note: to oust is to throw out and take the place of, so one letter replaces another

blocks.note: to revise is to change or amend
D is the standard abbreviation for Democrat
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A political scheme shifts when power passes from the Republicans to the Democrats.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the leading R of REVISE for D.
explanation.definitionFit: To devise something is to work out or invent a scheme, so the verb is a synonym for plan.

clue.text: Neutron, it’s briefly understood, has nuclear element

indicators.note: said briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: N is the symbol for a neutron
taken as written
radio-speak for 'message received and understood'
N is an abbreviation for nuclear

explanation.surface: A physics primer explains that a neutron is part of an atom's nucleus.
explanation.walkthrough: ROGER is what a radio operator says to mean 'understood'; cut short it loses its R. 'Element' alone is the definition, though 'nuclear element' reads as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is a chemical element, atomic number seven, making up most of the air we breathe.

clue.text: Ontarian athlete running around South Bank complex

indicators.note: running around suggests chaotic movement, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Canadian runner jogs laps around a building on London's riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: The South Bank is the arts district on the south side of the Thames in London; 'running around' looks like the athlete's activity but shuffles the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Theatre is a large concrete arts venue with several stages, built on London's South Bank in the 1970s.

clue.text: Vocal rebuke after country’s exchanging leaders for health food

indicators.note: coming after means placed later, fixing the order of the two parts
two words exchanging leaders swap their first letters with each other

blocks.note: Niger is a country in West Africa
the sound of disapproval made with the tongue

explanation.surface: Someone tuts at a nation that has swapped its rulers, all in aid of a diet product.
explanation.walkthrough: Put NIGER then TUT, then swap their first letters: N and T trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger nut is a small edible tuber sold as a fibre-rich snack and flour, marketed as a wholesome superfood.

clue.text: Volunteer dyke builder’s quoted by some

indicators.note: quoted means repeated in speech, and 'by some' admits only certain speakers say it this way

blocks.note: Offa was the Mercian king who built Offa's Dyke, the earthwork along the English-Welsh border

explanation.surface: A notice seeks someone willing to help build a sea wall, as some people report.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the final R is silent, so the two words sound the same; 'by some' concedes that rhotic speakers will not hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer is to put yourself forward or propose something freely, which is exactly what you do when you proffer help.

clue.text: Went past fell after leaving source of river

indicators.note: the source of a stream is where it starts, so only the opening letter is wanted
something leaving goes away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: to relapse is to fall back into illness after improving
first letter of the waterway

explanation.surface: A walker hurried past a hill once they had left the head of a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like a northern English hill beside a river, but it is the verb: 'fell after' recovering means relapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes or slips by, so elapsed is the past tense for time that went by.

clue.text: Dog with stick going around part of Ulster

indicators.note: going around something encircles it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a cane is a walking stick
Northern Ireland makes up six of Ulster's nine counties

explanation.surface: A dog fetching a stick roams around a corner of Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is the historic northern province of Ireland, most of which is Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Canine works as a noun for any member of the dog family, so it is a slightly formal synonym.

clue.text: Short nap in pulpit with arms splayed out

indicators.note: something made short has been cut, so its last letter goes
in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: kip is British slang for a sleep
an ambo is a raised reading desk or pulpit in early churches

explanation.surface: A preacher dozes off in the pulpit, sprawled with limbs flung wide.
explanation.walkthrough: AMBO is a church word solvers may not know: a raised stand from which scripture is read.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing akimbo means hands on hips with elbows jutting outward, the classic pose of arms bent out to the sides.

clue.text: Chill gloom returns after trade union contest

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run backwards
placed after means set later, fixing which part comes first

blocks.note: TU is the standard abbreviation for trade union
raw weather is cold and chilly
a fog is a murky darkness

explanation.surface: Dark feelings come back after a fight with the union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chill' and 'gloom' sound like the mood of the surface, but they are weather words: cold and murky. TU is the usual abbreviation for trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug-of-war is a team trial of strength pulling opposite ends of a rope, so it is a kind of contest.

clue.text: Red Hot Chili Peppers reviews I copy in duplicate

definitions.note: the band name is a plural phrase; the answer names the chilli

indicators.note: to re-view is to look back over, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to rip a CD is to copy it
the turned-round chunk written out a second time

explanation.surface: A critic of the American rock band duplicates their reviews.
explanation.walkthrough: The band's name looks like a red herring for music, but read literally it is red hot chilli peppers. I plus RIP, reversed, then doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Piri-piri is the small fiery African bird's-eye chilli, and the hot sauce made from it.

clue.text: Composition of Sartre's most exquisite

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: the French philosopher's name taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic praises a piece by the French existentialist as his finest.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in Sartre's is 'is', a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare can mean of unusual excellence, as in rare beauty, so the superlative matches most exquisite.

clue.text: Want soldiers to come back with leading seaman to port

indicators.note: coming back means returning the other way, so the letters run in reverse
leading means going in front, so this part is placed first

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman
to want is to need
RE, the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Troops long to return home with a senior sailor bound for a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading seaman' is a real naval rank, but here 'leading' just puts AB in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a major Scottish seaport on the North Sea, hub of the oil industry.

clue.text: A doctor nearly forced Mark to leave American diving exhibition

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut
leaving means going away, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: taken as written
a quack is a bogus doctor
made someone do it: forced them
M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A medic almost compelled a German to quit a US swimming show.
explanation.walkthrough: QUACK loses its K; MADE loses its M.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquacade is a US term for an entertainment of synchronised swimming and diving, often staged to music.

clue.text: Order book for hotshots

blocks.note: in biology, order and class are both ranks of classification; an order is a class or kind
Acts of the Apostles, a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone orders a book written for high flyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order book' looks like a ledger of sales, but the words split into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A class act is someone of outstanding quality or skill, the same as a hotshot or star performer.

clue.text: A bone, say, is processed for a source of oil

indicators.note: processing transforms raw material, so the letters are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bones are rendered down at a factory to extract oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' usually signals an example or a sound, but here it is plain letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The legume is pressed to produce one of the world's most widely used vegetable cooking oils.

clue.text: Continue with office call

blocks.note: to last is to go on or continue
a post is an office or position held

explanation.surface: An employee is told to carry on working with a phone call at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' looks like a phone call but is a bugle call.
explanation.definitionFit: The Last Post is the military bugle signal sounded at nightfall and at remembrance ceremonies.

clue.text: A marriage partner's accepting last part of wedding contract

indicators.note: the last part of a word is its final letter alone
accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a bride is a partner in a marriage; the 's is 'is'
final letter of the ceremony

explanation.surface: A spouse signs up to the final clause of a marriage agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like the noun for a wedding agreement; it is the verb meaning shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten or condense it, which is one sense of the verb contract.

clue.text: Together stop sanctions ending increasingly early

indicators.note: each word stops sooner than the one before, so successive words lose more letters from the end

blocks.note: to stop is to end; it loses one letter
sanctions block trade; it loses two letters

explanation.surface: Nations unite to halt penalties that keep finishing sooner and sooner.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word is cut by one letter and the second by two: 'increasingly' early.
explanation.definitionFit: En bloc is a French borrowing meaning all at once, as a single unit, so it means together.

clue.text: NY cops put in cooler

blocks.note: the heat is American slang for the police
to sink a ball is to put it in the hole or pocket

explanation.surface: New York police throw someone in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' is slang for prison, which completes the cop picture, but here it means a device that cools.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat sink is a finned metal component that draws heat away from electronics, a passive cooling device.

clue.text: A cross celebrity stands up guitar player

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
an X is a cross shape
a big name is a celebrity

explanation.surface: An irritated star gets to their feet against the guitarist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry, but it is the letter shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Axe is slang for an electric guitar, so an axeman is a guitarist, especially a rock lead player.

clue.text: Greek secretary knocked over Pascal’s drink

indicators.note: something knocked over is turned the other way, so the letters are flipped

blocks.note: GR is an abbreviation for Greek
a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary
Pa is the symbol for the pascal, the SI unit of pressure

explanation.surface: A Greek assistant spilt the French thinker's glass.
explanation.walkthrough: Pascal looks like the philosopher, but it is the unit of pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian brandy distilled from grape pomace, a strong spirit drunk after meals.

clue.text: Philosopher embraced by reflection of total peace

indicators.note: what is embraced is held inside, so the letters sit within the phrase
a mirror reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: read backwards, the letters inside spell the philosopher

explanation.surface: A sage is held within a calm meditation on universal harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'total peace' from right to left and the name appears across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Athenian thinker, pupil of Socrates and author of The Republic.

clue.text: Accommodating article about Maine’s expert

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: an indefinite article
ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine; the 's is 'has'
able means skilled

explanation.surface: A helpful newspaper piece on a skilled specialist from New England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a piece of writing, but in crosswords it is usually A, AN or THE. ME is the US postal code for Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenable person is willing and easy to persuade, a near synonym of obliging and accommodating.

clue.text: Touching US promotion for bargain basement tuxedos!

blocks.note: a DJ, dinner jacket, is the British name for a tuxedo; priced per item
a cent, a rock-bottom American price

explanation.surface: A moving American advert offers formal wear at knockdown prices.
explanation.walkthrough: The promotion's slogan reads 'A DJ, A CENT!': one dinner jacket for one cent. A DJ, short for dinner jacket, is the British word for a tuxedo.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacent means lying next to or in contact with something, so it works as a synonym for touching.

clue.text: Join offensive to oust King Henry

indicators.note: ousting means pushing out and taking the place of, so one letter replaces another

blocks.note: an offensive is an attack
H is the symbol for the henry, the SI unit of inductance
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Rebels enlist in a campaign to depose a Tudor monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Henry' reads as one monarch but splits in two: K goes out, H comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach is to fasten or connect one thing to another, the same as join.

clue.text: Criticise musicians housed by Wally

indicators.note: what is housed is sheltered inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a wally is British slang for a fool
ENO, the English National Opera

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a band who are living with a buffoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally looks like a name, but in British slang a wally is an idiot. ENO is the London opera company.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to condemn publicly, a stronger form of criticise.
